key_insight: Post-optimization corrections can substantially improve optimized ADAPT-VQE results without adding new ansatz layers or re-running nonlinear optimization.
engineering_relevance: These methods lower circuit depth and measurement cost for quantum chemistry, making variational quantum algorithms more practical on near-term hardware.
method: Apply Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization to the optimized ADAPT-VQE state.
Use identity-augmented q-sc-EOM to recover accuracy from truncated or sampled-ranked ansätze.
Avoid further ansatz growth and additional gradient-based operator selection after optimization.
evidence_signal: Across molecular systems up to 20 qubits, Krylov correction reduced the iterations needed to reach the 1.6 mEh threshold by up to about 6× and lowered measurement cost by up to about 40× under a resource-cost model.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the optimized starting state and on the chosen resource-cost model, so gains may vary across molecules and hardware settings.
paper_title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
